title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 122 (Applicability of this Chapter to One Person Company)

content.overview: The provisions of section 98 and sections 100 to 111 (both inclusive) shall not apply to a One Person Company. Ordinary business under section 102(2)(a) that other companies transact at an AGM shall, in the case of an OPC, be transacted as provided in section 122(3). The sole member communicates the resolution to the company and enters it in the minute book, signed and dated by the member; the date of signature is treated as the date of the meeting for this purpose.
content.glance: Sections 98 and 100–111 do not apply to an OPC; the sole member records and signs decisions in the minute book as required.
content.study:
## Section 122 — Applicability to One Person Company

**Excluded provisions.** Section 122(1) provides that sections 98 and 100 to 111 do not apply to an OPC. Use the exact statutory list; do not assume a blanket exemption from every meeting-related requirement.

**Sole-member decision.** In the circumstances specified by the section, business that would otherwise be transacted at a general meeting may be dealt with by the member communicating the resolution to the company. The resolution must be entered in the minute book and signed and dated by the member; the date of signature is treated as the date of the meeting.

**Limits.** Section 122 does not remove every obligation under the Companies Act. Apply provisions not excluded by section 122 and the applicable rules.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.
